summary: iter128 close-out — verified Dispatch User impersonation (admin → mints X-Dispatch-Token without re-login) and Pending Maintenance Hold approval/dismissal workflow end-to-end. 12 new backend tests + 56 regression tests (iter122 + iter123 + iter124 + iter126) → 68/68 PASSED. Frontend verified: /admin/people Dispatch Users panel renders with correct 'Dispatch Portal' / 'Dispatch Users & Logins' headers (no stale 'Safety' wording), ROLE_OPTIONS = ['Dispatcher', 'Dispatch Manager', 'Operations Coordinator', 'Other'] (4 entries, no duplicates), each row has per-user 'View as Dispatcher' eye button (data-testid='admin-dispatch-view-as-{id}'). Clicking it shows a confirm() prompt, stashes the minted dispatch token in localStorage['masci.dispatch.token'] + user, and opens /dispatch-portal in a new tab. /admin/dispatch → Holds tab renders the amber 'Pending Maintenance / Safety Holds — admin review required' card (data-testid='dp-pending-holds') with per-row Approve / Dismiss buttons; approving a pending hold removes it from the pending list and moves it into the active holds table below. No regressions detected.
critical_code_review_comments: dispatch_portal_auth.py: impersonate endpoint correctly handles the no-password-yet case by bootstrapping a random unrecoverable secret + must_change=True — clean fallback, prevents 500s on users created but never password-issued.

operations.py: HoldDismiss.reason is min_length=2 → Pydantic returns 422 on missing/short reason, matching review-request spec exactly. The redundant runtime check (`if not body.reason.strip()`) inside dismiss_hold is dead code but harmless.
operations.py approve_hold treats status=None as 'pending' (legacy holds created before the status field existed will still be approvable). Smart compat handling.

AdminDispatchUsersPanel.jsx: viewAsDispatcher() uses window.confirm() (blocks UI) — adequate for an admin-only preview action but could be upgraded to a styled modal for parity with other destructive confirms. Low-priority polish.
Audit event uses __import__('datetime').datetime.now(...) inline — works but ugly; could be hoisted to a module-level _now_iso helper (already exists in operations.py) for consistency. Cosmetic only.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter128 closes out P1-P4 Enterprise Operations Architecture. Backend: impersonation route at /api/admin/dispatch-users/{id}/impersonate is admin-gated, returns {token,user}, 404 on unknown id, 409 on disabled user, audit-logs to db.audit_events.
